title: Install Hazri and first run
intro: First run is three short screens: Welcome, your language, and how you read Gurbani. None of them is an account. There is no sign-up, no password and no login, and it takes under a minute.

steps.title: Get Hazri on your Android phone
steps.body: Hazri is coming soon to Google Play, for Android 7.0 or later. Leave your email on the Download page and we will write once, on launch day. Then install it like any other app.

steps.title: Answer Android’s notification question
steps.body: On Android 13 and newer, Android asks the first time Hazri opens whether it may send notifications. Allow lets the 4:00 AM Amrit Vela reminder and your goal reminders arrive. Setup carries on whichever you choose.

steps.title: Read Welcome, then tap Begin
steps.body: Welcome shows one day with Hazri as a timeline: the Amrit Vela reminder, the hazri marked, a daily goal, a sangat group and the streak kept in your diary. It is an illustration, not your data.

steps.title: Choose your language
steps.body: Pick ਪੰਜਾਬੀ, हिन्दी or English for the app. You can change it any time in Settings.

steps.title: Choose how you read Gurbani
steps.body: Pick Gurmukhi, Devanagari or Roman, each shown with the first line of Japji Sahib, and set the text size. Elder mode is here too, for larger text and simpler screens. It is already on if your phone’s text is set large. Skip, at the top, finishes setup with Gurmukhi at the standard size.
steps.where: How do you like to read Gurbani?

steps.title: You are on Today
steps.body: Today opens with a Welcome greeting, a Set up your profile banner you can ignore, the hazri banner and the Set a daily goal card. Everything on it works with no signal.

tip: You never need a profile to read, listen, get reminders or keep a diary. Make one later only if you want to be on the globe, the weekly backup or a sangat group of your own.

faq.q: Do I need an account to use Hazri?
faq.a: No. There is no sign-up, no password and no sign-in screen. A profile is optional. You can make one later from the Set up your profile banner on Today.

faq.q: I said no to notifications. Can I change it?
faq.a: Yes. Open the menu and tap Notifications. A card there has an Allow button. It asks again, or opens Android’s notification settings for Hazri if Android will not ask a second time.

faq.q: Can I change the language or script after setup?
faq.a: Yes. Menu › Settings has App language, Gurbani script and Text size, and Elder mode is under Display. Inside a bani, ਅ / अ / A switches the script too.

title: Mark your daily Hazri
intro: Hazri means presence. One finished paath of any bani, or one sitting of Naam Simran of five minutes or more, marks the day. It needs no goal, no profile and no signal.

steps.title: Look at the hazri banner
steps.body: Near the top of Today the banner says Today’s hazri is not marked yet, and what marks it: one paath, or one sitting of simran.

steps.title: Finish any bani
steps.body: Tap the main button on Today, such as Start my Nitnem, or open the Nitnem tab and choose a bani. Reading to the last line and staying there five seconds counts. So does the recitation playing to the end.

steps.title: Or sit for five minutes
steps.body: On the Simran tab tap Begin Simran. A sitting of five minutes or more marks hazri, even if your goal’s sitting is longer and you end it early after five.

steps.title: See it marked
steps.body: The banner turns green with a tick: Today’s hazri is marked, with the time and what marked it, such as Marked at 5:52 AM, with Japji Sahib. The Diary shows an orange dot for today. Once it is marked you can close the banner for the rest of the day.

steps.title: Did your paath away from the app?
steps.body: Open the Diary, tap today and use + beside the bani under Add or take away. It marks hazri in the same way. Today and the 7 days before it can be changed.

tip: Reading and listening to the same bani in one opening count once. Reading it again later in the day is another paath, and both are kept in your Diary.

faq.q: Does Ardas or Sukhmani Sahib count?
faq.a: Yes. Finishing any bani in the app marks the day, Ardas and Sukhmani Sahib included.

faq.q: Does a sitting shorter than five minutes count?
faq.a: It is kept in your Diary, but it does not mark hazri. A sitting of five minutes or more does.

faq.q: When does a new day start?
faq.a: At midnight on your phone. The banner comes back unmarked the next morning, and the day you marked stays in your Diary.

title: Read and listen to a bani with the recitation
intro: Every bani in Hazri comes with a recitation, and the text follows it line by line. It plays from the phone, so it works with no signal and keeps going with the screen locked.

steps.title: Open a bani
steps.body: On the Nitnem tab, tap a bani such as Japji Sahib. It opens at the line where you left off, and the list shows how far in you are, such as 2:04 in.

steps.title: Choose your script and text
steps.body: ਅ / अ / A switches between Gurmukhi, Devanagari and Roman. Aa opens Text settings: text size, Show meanings and their language, Roman under Gurmukhi, Pause marks (vishraam), Larivaar, Keep screen on while reading and Follow audio.

steps.title: Press play and follow along
steps.body: Tap play in the player at the bottom. The line being recited is highlighted and the page scrolls with the paath. Scroll away and the player says Auto-scroll paused, and a Back to paath pill appears. Tap either to return. Tap any line to move the paath there.

steps.title: Set the speed and a sleep timer
steps.body: The speed button on the player switches between 1.0× and 1.5× with one tap. The clock button opens Speed, from 0.75× to 1.5× with the pitch kept the same, and Sleep timer: Off, 15, 30 or 60 min. When the timer runs out the paath fades out over five seconds.

steps.title: Lock the phone
steps.body: The paath keeps playing. The notification and lock screen carry previous, back 10 seconds, play and pause, forward 10 seconds and next, and Bluetooth and headset buttons work. A phone call pauses it and it carries on when the call ends. Unplugging headphones pauses it rather than switching to the speaker.

steps.title: Start again, or go on
steps.body: At the end a card says the bani is complete and Logged in your diary, with the time. Start again takes you to the first line, puts the recitation back to the start and clears where you left off. Next bani opens the next one in the same section. After the last one it says Back to Nitnem.

tip: If play and pause do not show on the lock screen, notifications are off for Hazri. The reader says Lock-screen controls are off, with Allow, and Settings › Audio › Lock-screen controls says which.

faq.q: Do I have to listen for the paath to count?
faq.a: No. Reading to the last line and staying there five seconds counts, and so does the recitation reaching the end. Doing both in one opening counts once.

faq.q: Why is there no Hindi meaning for some banis?
faq.a: Meanings come only from the sources carried in the app, and nothing is machine-translated to fill a gap. English covers every bani and Punjabi nearly all of them. Hindi is there for some banis only.

faq.q: Does the recitation use mobile data?
faq.a: No. Every recitation is stored in the app and played from the phone. Nothing is streamed.

title: Play all for the morning Nitnem
intro: Play all plays the five Amrit Vela banis one after another, so the morning Nitnem needs no tapping between banis. Each one that plays to the end counts as a paath of its own.

steps.title: Open the Nitnem tab
steps.body: The Amrit Vela section lists Japji Sahib, Jaap Sahib, Tav Prasad Savaiye, Chaupai Sahib and Anand Sahib, with how long they take together under the heading, such as 5 banis · about 66 min.

steps.title: Tap Play all
steps.body: The navy Play all button sits beside the heading. The recitation starts with Japji Sahib and moves through the five in order, with no gap between them. You stay on the list.

steps.title: Listen from any tab
steps.body: A strip at the bottom of the app shows the bani playing and its time, with pause and stop. The notification and lock screen show the bani’s name and, under it, Morning Nitnem · 1 of 5, then the line being recited.

steps.title: Leave it playing
steps.body: Lock the phone or switch apps and it carries on. Next and previous on the lock screen, and on Bluetooth and headset buttons, move between the banis. A phone call pauses it, and it carries on when the call ends.

steps.title: Each bani counts
steps.body: Each bani whose recitation reaches the end is one paath. The first one marks your hazri, and each counts toward your goal and toward any sangat group you are in for that bani. The Diary lists them as Listened.

tip: Play all is made for listening. To read along with one bani, open it from the list and press play there. Reading along and listening to the same bani count once between them.

faq.q: Is there a Play all for the evening?
faq.a: Play all shows on a section with more than one recitation. Evening has Rehras Sahib and Bedtime has Kirtan Sohila, one bani each, so you open those directly. More banis has Play all for Ardas and Sukhmani Sahib.

faq.q: How do I stop it?
faq.a: Tap pause on the strip at the bottom, or × beside it to stop. The pause on the lock screen works too.

faq.q: Does it need a signal?
faq.a: No. All five recitations are stored in the app and play from the phone.

title: Set your daily paath goal
intro: A goal is your own list for each day: any bani a number of times, and Naam Simran by the minute if you like, each with its own length and reminder. Today shows how it stands and the Diary keeps every day.

steps.title: Tap Set a daily goal
steps.body: On Today, the Set a daily goal card opens the Add to your goal sheet.

steps.title: Choose a bani or Naam Simran
steps.body: Japji Sahib, Chaupai Sahib, Anand Sahib, Rehras Sahib and Sukhmani Sahib come first, and More… lists every other bani. Naam Simran is counted in minutes. A bani already in your goal says In your goal, and choosing it edits that item.

steps.title: Say how much
steps.body: For a bani, set Times a day from 1 to 11 with − and +. For Naam Simran, pick 5, 11, 21 or 31 min, or Custom for anything from 5 to 120.

steps.title: Say for how long
steps.body: Every day; For 40 days, which − and + change to anything from 1 to 365; or Until a date up to a year away.

steps.title: Add a reminder
steps.body: Reminders start off. Switch Reminder on and pick a time; it starts at 7:30 PM. It comes only on days the item is not yet done, with In 15 min to snooze. If Android has not allowed on-time reminders, a card here offers Allow on-time reminders.

steps.title: Save it
steps.body: Tap Add to goal. Today now shows Today’s goal with a ring, how many are done, and one row per item. Tap a row to start it: a bani opens in the reader, Naam Simran opens the Simran tab.

steps.title: Change or remove an item
steps.body: Tap the top of the goal card on Today, or Menu › Settings › Paath goals, to open My paath goals. Each item’s menu has Edit and Remove. Removing it takes it out of your goal from today, and days already recorded stay as they are.

tip: The goal is met on a day when every item in it is done, and Today says All of today’s goals are done once that day. Hazri is separate: one paath marks it, goal or no goal.

faq.q: Can my goal have more than one bani?
faq.a: Yes. Add as many items as you like with Add to goal. Each has its own times a day, length and reminder.

faq.q: What happens when a For 40 days item ends?
faq.a: It leaves your goal after its last day. When every item has ended, Today shows Set a daily goal again with Your last goal is complete. Set a new one.

faq.q: Does a paath beyond my target count for anything?
faq.a: Every paath is kept in your Diary. For the goal, an item is done once it reaches its number for the day.

title: Turn on on-time reminders
intro: Hazri plans every reminder on the phone, so they arrive with no signal. For them to arrive on time, Android needs to allow notifications and, on newer phones, Alarms & reminders. Some phones need one battery setting as well.

steps.title: Allow notifications
steps.body: On Android 13 and newer, Android asks when Hazri first opens. If you said no, open the menu and tap Notifications. A card says reminders need permission to show notifications, with an Allow button. It asks again, or opens Android’s notification settings for Hazri.

steps.title: Allow on-time reminders
steps.body: If Android has not allowed Hazri Alarms & reminders, the same screen says reminders can arrive late, sometimes by hours. Tap Allow on-time reminders, switch it on for Hazri on the page Android opens, and come back. The card goes once it is allowed.

steps.title: Choose what Hazri sends
steps.body: One switch each, all on until you turn one off. Amrit Vela, every day at 4:00 AM. Goal reminders, at the time you set on each goal. Gurpurab and Sikh events, on the day: Gurpurabs at 6:00 AM, other days at 7:00 AM. Hazri reminder, at 7:00 AM, only with no goal and no Hazri yet. Once you are in a sangat group, Sangat too: your groups at 9:00 PM, and their milestones.

steps.title: Let Hazri run in the background
steps.body: Some phones stop background apps to save battery. Reminders not arriving? in Settings gives the steps for Samsung, Xiaomi, Vivo, Oppo and OnePlus.

steps.title: Test it
steps.body: Diagnostics shows whether notifications and exact alarms are allowed, whether battery optimisation is off for Hazri, and what is planned next. Send one now shows one at once. Send one in two minutes tests a real reminder. If battery optimisation is still on, Let Hazri run in the background opens Android’s setting.

steps.title: Snooze when you need to
steps.body: A goal reminder carries In 15 min. It comes back once, fifteen minutes later.

tip: A reminder due while you are sitting for Naam Simran waits until the sitting ends, so nothing interrupts it.

faq.q: Why is there no Sangat switch?
faq.a: It shows only once you are in a sangat group.

faq.q: Will a goal reminder still come after I have done the paath?
faq.a: No. A goal reminder is not sent on a day that item is already done, and one already showing is taken away once you finish it.

faq.q: Can I turn off the reminder for one Gurpurab?
faq.a: Yes. Open the Gurpurab calendar from its card on Today and tap the bell beside that day. The same bell turns a reminder on for a day that has none.

title: Sit for Naam Simran and see the globe
intro: A sitting of Naam Simran is five quiet minutes, or your goal’s length, with a recitation of Waheguru. Around it, the globe shows the sangat of the day, city by city.

steps.title: Open the Simran tab
steps.body: The globe turns slowly, with how many are live today under it and the legend: You, Live and Here today. You can turn it with your finger.

steps.title: Tap Begin Simran
steps.body: The button shows the length: the minutes of the Naam Simran item in your goal, or 5 minutes when there is none.

steps.title: Sit
steps.body: The recitation plays and a countdown takes the place of the live count. Pause holds the clock and the recitation together, and Resume carries on. End finishes the sitting early.

steps.title: Finish
steps.body: When the time is up the sitting ends by itself and says Simran complete, logged in your Diary. A sitting of 5 minutes or more marks hazri. It meets a Naam Simran goal only at the goal’s minutes. A sitting ended early is kept, marked stopped early.

steps.title: Read the globe
steps.body: Your city blinks orange. Green dots are people who opened Hazri today, and blue dots are the others on the globe who have not yet. A dot grows with its city’s count, and threads join you to every other dot. It refreshes every 2 minutes while you look.

steps.title: Put yourself on it
steps.body: Without a profile there is no orange dot, and the threads join all the dots into one web. Tap the banner under the legend to set up a profile.
steps.tap: Create your profile to see yourself on the globe

tip: The globe shows a city and a count, never a name. The sitting itself never needs a signal.

faq.q: How do I sit for longer than five minutes?
faq.a: Add Naam Simran to your goal with the minutes you want, from 5 to 120. Begin Simran then uses that length. The recitation itself lasts five minutes, and in a longer sitting the countdown carries on after it.

faq.q: Can I sit again after today’s sitting?
faq.a: Yes. After a full sitting the button says Done today ✓. Tap it to begin another, and the Diary keeps each one.

faq.q: Why does the globe say it can’t reach the sangat?
faq.a: The globe is the one part of this screen that needs a connection. Without one it says Can’t reach the sangat right now. Your sitting still works and is still logged.

title: Use the Diary and your streak
intro: The Diary is every day at a glance: whether hazri was marked, whether the goal was met, and each paath of the day. Your streak shows how many days of hazri in a row, now and at its longest.

steps.title: Open the Diary tab
steps.body: Nitnem Diary shows the month, with today ringed. An orange dot is a day with hazri. A second dot appears only on days that had a goal: green when it was met, grey when not. The arrows beside the month move between months.

steps.title: Read your streak
steps.body: Once your longest run is 2 days or more, a card shows days in a row now and your longest. Below two days now, only the longest shows, and nothing ever says a streak ended. From 2 days in a row, Today shows the same streak with the last seven days.

steps.title: Let grace days work
steps.body: Two grace days a month bridge a single missed day, so the streak keeps going. They are given on their own and show as GRACE on that day. They keep the run going without adding to it.

steps.title: Tap a day
steps.body: The day shows Hazri marked or No hazri, with the time and what marked it. On a day with a goal it shows Goal: 1 of 2 met. Under Recited is every bani with its times and whether it was Read, Listened or Marked in Diary, and every sitting of Naam Simran.

steps.title: Add or take away a paath
steps.body: For today and the 7 days before it, every bani and Naam Simran has + and −. Use + for a paath done away from the app; − takes away the newest one. Older days say: Days more than 7 days ago can’t be changed.
steps.where: Diary › a day › Add or take away

steps.title: See the month’s numbers
steps.body: Under the grid: hazri days and goals met for the month.

tip: In a sangat group, at most three paath added with + count toward the group each day. Your own Diary is never capped.

faq.q: What counts toward my streak?
faq.a: A day with hazri: any finished paath, or a sitting of Naam Simran of five minutes or more. Meeting the goal is not needed.

faq.q: Does adding a sitting with + mark hazri?
faq.a: Yes. A sitting added with + takes the length of your Naam Simran goal, and never less than five minutes, so it marks hazri for that day.

faq.q: Does the Diary need the internet?
faq.a: No. The Diary is kept on your phone and works with no signal.

title: Join a built-in sangat
intro: Three built-in groups are open to everyone: Amrit Vela Sangat, Simran Sangat and Sukhmani Sahib Sangat. Each has one goal at a time. Join one and every matching paath you finish counts toward it, with no profile needed. Joining needs a connection.

steps.title: Open the Sangat tab
steps.body: Scroll down to Join the sangat. Each built-in group shows its goal on one line, its member count and a Join button.

steps.title: Tap Join
steps.body: You are in at once, and the button changes to Leave. Without a profile you show to other members as Sangat member. Make a profile later and your membership and everything you added move to it.

steps.title: Open the group
steps.body: Tap the group’s name. The ring shows the total against the target. Under This goal are three points: when it started, today with the days left, and when it ends and the next goal starts.

steps.title: Sit for the paath
steps.body: Sit for Naam Simran opens the Simran tab. For a bani the button carries the bani’s name and opens the reader. A paath of that bani counts wherever you start it, from the day you joined.

steps.title: See what you added
steps.body: Three figures: Sangat today, Yours today and Yours toward the goal. Under Members, everyone is listed A to Z with their own figure. There is never a ranking.

steps.title: Leave any time
steps.body: Tap Leave on the group’s row in the Sangat tab, or open the group menu and tap Leave. What you contributed stays in the group’s total, and you can join again whenever you like.

tip: Offline, your paath waits safely on the phone and goes up when you are back. When a built-in goal ends, met or not, a new one starts the next day.

faq.q: Does a paath I add in the Diary count?
faq.a: Yes, up to 3 a day in each group. A paath you read or play in the app, and a Simran sitting, has no such limit.

faq.q: How are Naam Simran minutes counted?
faq.a: Each sitting adds its whole minutes. A sitting of 7 minutes 59 seconds adds 7, and one under a minute adds nothing.

faq.q: Does paath from before I joined count?
faq.a: No. A group counts paath from the day you join, and only while its goal is running.

title: Create your own sangat group and set a goal
intro: A group of your own is private: for your family, your gurdwara or your friends. Only the people you invite can find it. It has one goal, so many paath of one bani or so many minutes of Naam Simran, and an end date.

steps.title: Make a profile first
steps.body: Creating a group needs a profile. Without one, Create group says: Create your profile to start a group of your own, with a Set up your profile button.

steps.title: Tap Create group
steps.body: On the Sangat tab, the navy tile at the top: Create group, One goal, an end date.

steps.title: Name the group
steps.body: Type a Group name of up to 64 characters, in any script, such as Gill Parivar. Only its members see it.

steps.title: Set the goal
steps.body: Under Set the goal, choose Paath of one bani and pick it from Choose a bani, or choose Naam Simran. Enter the Target, from 1 to 1,000,000 paath or minutes. Ends on is filled in for you; tap it to choose any day up to a year away. Then tap Create.

steps.title: Know what can change
steps.body: The goal can’t be changed later; only its end date can. Use Change end date in the group menu. To end early, set it to today.

steps.title: Share the invite
steps.body: Hazri opens your new group with Share invite ready. The next guide covers the link and the code.

steps.title: Look after the group
steps.body: The group menu has Reset invite code, and Delete group while you are still the only member. To remove someone, tap the person icon on their row under Members, then Remove from group. You can run up to 5 active groups at once.

tip: An example: Gill Parivar, 1,100 Japji Sahib by 30 Nov. When the target is reached the group ends at once, and its history stays for every member to open.

faq.q: Can I leave a group I started?
faq.a: No. The person who starts a group stays in it. You can end it early by changing the end date to today, or delete it while you are the only member.

faq.q: What if I want more than 5 groups?
faq.a: Only active groups count, so a group that has ended frees a place. To run more at once, write to support@hazri.me.

faq.q: Can someone in the group change the goal?
faq.a: No. Nobody can change the goal once it is set. Only you, as the person who started the group, can change its end date.

title: Invite family with a link or code
intro: Anyone in an active private group can invite others with a link or an eight-character code. Joining needs no approval and no profile, and the person can be new to Hazri.

steps.title: Tap Share invite
steps.body: Open the group and tap Share invite under the members, or choose it from the group menu. Android’s share sheet opens with a message holding the group’s name and goal, a link and the code. You choose the app.

steps.title: Know the code
steps.body: Eight letters and numbers, shown like K7QM-4XPA, with no 0, O, 1, I or L to confuse. A code lasts 30 days. Sharing again reuses it while it is valid, and makes a new one once it has run out.

steps.title: With Hazri installed
steps.body: Tapping the link opens Hazri on Join a group, with You have an invite to a group and the code filled in. Tap Join.

steps.title: Without Hazri
steps.body: The link opens a page that shows the code large, with Copy the code and Get Hazri. Installing from Get Hazri carries the code along: after the first-run screens, Hazri opens Join a group with the code already in.

steps.title: Type a code instead
steps.body: On the Sangat tab, tap the Join group tile. Type the code under Invite code, or tap Paste code. It works with or without the hyphen, in any case, and from a whole pasted message. Hazri reads your clipboard only when you tap Paste code.

steps.title: If it does not work
steps.body: This code isn't valid. Ask for a new invite. means the code is mistyped, out of date or replaced. The person who started the group can make a fresh one with Reset invite code, which stops the old code at once. You may also see This group is full. or This group has ended.

tip: Already in the group? The code simply opens it.

faq.q: Does the person need a profile to join?
faq.a: No. They join as Sangat member, and their name shows once they make a profile.

faq.q: Can I invite people to a built-in group?
faq.a: No. Built-in groups have no invite, because anyone can join them with Join on the Sangat tab.

faq.q: How many people can join?
faq.a: Up to 1,000 in a group of your own.

title: Make a profile and verify your email
intro: A profile is optional. It greets you by name, puts your city on the Simran globe, backs up your goals and diary every week and lets you start a sangat group. There is no password: your email is confirmed with a link.

steps.title: Tap Set up your profile
steps.body: On Today, tap the Set up your profile banner. The menu has a Set up your profile row too.

steps.title: Fill in the four fields
steps.body: Name *, Email * and City * are needed. Phone (optional) is not. Your name can be 2 to 50 letters. Choose your city from the list; if it is not there, choose the nearest city.

steps.title: Tap Save Profile
steps.body: Profile saved asks whether you would like to confirm your email. It is optional, and Skip for now takes you back to Today.

steps.title: Open the link on this phone
steps.body: Check your email shows where the link went. Open the mail on this phone and tap the link within 24 hours; Hazri shows Email verified. Resend link appears after a minute, and Wrong email? Change it fixes a typo.

steps.title: See what changed
steps.body: Today now says Welcome with your name. The person icon in the navy band opens Your profile, with your days of Hazri, how many in a row and your badges. Your city joins the globe, and the weekly backup starts from the next Sunday.

steps.title: Edit it later
steps.body: Your profile › Edit profile changes your name and city, and Change email changes the address. A new email takes over only once you confirm it from the link we send. Then tap Save changes.

tip: No password, ever. Your email is never shown to anyone in the app. Your city is one dot on the Simran globe, and nothing finer.

faq.q: I skipped confirming my email. Can I do it later?
faq.a: Yes. Your profile shows Not verified beside your email, with Confirm my email and Change email under it.

faq.q: It says Email already registered. What now?
faq.a: That email already has a profile, made on this phone or another one. Tap Send link and open the mail on this phone within 1 hour to bring that profile back here.

faq.q: What do people in my groups see?
faq.a: Your name, in place of Sangat member, and what you added to the group’s goal. Never your email, your phone or your city.

title: Back up and restore your goals and diary
intro: With a profile, Hazri backs up your goals, every paath and Simran sitting in your Diary, and your badges once a week. It can bring them back on this phone or on a new one.

steps.title: Make sure you have a profile
steps.body: The backup runs only with a profile, because a profile is what it is restored to.

steps.title: Let it run on its own
steps.body: Every Sunday, between midnight and 1 am, Hazri sends what changed since the last backup. If the phone was off or offline then, it runs once the phone is back online or when you next open Hazri.

steps.title: Or tap Back up now
steps.body: Your profile › Back up now runs it at once and says Backed up. The line under the buttons gives the date and time of the last backup, or Not backed up yet.

steps.title: Restore on this phone
steps.body: Tap Restore my goals and diary. Restore from backup? says it adds your goals and diary from the backup and removes nothing already on this phone, and gives the backup’s date. Tap Restore.

steps.title: On a new phone
steps.body: After first run, fill in Set up profile with the same email. Email already registered offers Send link; open the mail on the new phone within 1 hour. Profile restored then offers Restore my goals and diary straight away.

steps.title: Know what it covers
steps.body: The copy is as of the last backup; anything after that is not included. Your sangat groups are not in it: they come back with the profile itself. Reminders and settings are not backed up.

tip: Changing phones? Tap Back up now on the old one first, so the copy is up to the minute.

faq.q: Does a restore overwrite what is on the phone?
faq.a: No. It adds what the phone does not have, and updates an entry only where the backup’s copy is newer. Nothing on the phone is removed.

faq.q: What if I clear the app’s data without a profile?
faq.a: Then there is nothing to restore. Without a profile, your goals and diary live only on this phone.

faq.q: What happens on the old phone?
faq.a: Once your profile is restored on the new phone, the old one stops backing up.

title: Share Today’s Vichar as an image
intro: Each day Today carries one line from Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji with its meaning: Today’s Vichar. Everyone sees the same line on the same date, and you can send it on as a picture or as text.

steps.title: Find the card on Today
steps.body: Scroll Today past your goals and the button for your next paath. The card is headed Today’s Vichar, Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji.

steps.title: Read it in full
steps.body: Explore, or a tap on the card, opens the line with its meaning In Punjabi and In English.

steps.title: Tap Share
steps.body: It is on the card and at the foot of the full page. Share this Vichar asks how to send it.

steps.title: Choose As image
steps.body: A cream card with ਅੱਜ ਦਾ ਵਿਚਾਰ at the top, the line, its meaning, Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji and Read daily on Hazri. It suits a family chat or a status. As text sends the same as plain words.

steps.title: Pick the app
steps.body: Android’s share sheet opens. Choose the app, then who to send it to.

tip: The 200 lines ship with the app, so the card is there with no signal. After 200 days they begin again.

faq.q: I can’t see the card on Today.
faq.a: Elder mode leaves the Vichar card off Today. Turn Elder mode off in Settings › Display to see it again.

faq.q: Is Vichar in the menu the same thing?
faq.a: No. Vichar in the menu is a library of articles, and it needs a connection. Today’s Vichar is the one line on Today.

faq.q: Which language is the meaning in?
faq.a: On the card and the image, English when the app is in English, and Punjabi otherwise. The full page shows both Punjabi and English.

title: Earn badges
intro: Ten badges mark steps in the practice, counted in days from your own Diary. There are no points and no progress bars, nothing is ever taken away, and a badge never arrives as a notification.

steps.title: Open Badges
steps.body: Open the menu and tap Badges, or its navy header, which shows the badges you have. Your profile shows all ten too, with See all 10.

steps.title: Read the page
steps.body: The top line says how many of the 10 you have earned and on how many days you marked Hazri. Each badge shows its name, its rule, and Earned with a date, or Not yet.

steps.title: Tap a badge
steps.body: Each opens on its own page, Badge 1 of 10 and on, with What it marks and How it is earned, and the previous and next badge at the foot.

steps.title: Earn them in days
steps.body: Jigyasu: your first hazri. Shardhalu: Hazri on 7 days. Abhyasi: Hazri on 40 days. Nitnemi: the five morning banis, all on the same day, on 40 days. Simrani: Simran of 5 minutes or more on 108 days. Paathi: every bani in the app read or heard through once. Gursikh: Nitnemi, Simrani, Paathi and Hazri on 180 days. Vichari: Hazri on 365 days. The days need not be in a row.

steps.title: The two sangat badges
steps.body: Sevadar: be part of 3 sangat goals that are reached, with at least one paath of your own in each. Satsangi: 5 people join groups you created. Both need a profile.

steps.title: When one is earned
steps.body: A quiet New badge sheet appears the next time you are on a tab, never over the reader or a Simran sitting. Tap Done, or See all badges.

tip: Badges are part of the weekly backup, so a restore brings them back on a new phone.

faq.q: Can I lose a badge?
faq.a: No. Nothing is ever taken away. Removing a paath from the Diary later leaves a badge where it is.

faq.q: Does a paath I mark in the Diary count?
faq.a: Yes. A paath read from a gutka and marked with the Diary’s + counts like any other.

faq.q: Do I need a profile for badges?
faq.a: Only for Sevadar and Satsangi. The other eight need nothing but your Diary.

title: Elder mode, dark mode and languages
intro: Hazri can be larger, darker and in your language. Elder mode keeps the same screens with extra-large text and big buttons.

steps.title: Open Settings
steps.body: Tap the menu button at the top left of any tab, then Settings.

steps.title: Turn on Elder mode
steps.body: Display › Elder mode: Extra-large text and big buttons. Today keeps the same order, larger, and the Vichar and Gurpurab cards step aside.

steps.title: Choose a theme
steps.body: Display › Theme: Auto follows your phone, or choose Light or Dark.

steps.title: Change the app language
steps.body: Language › App language: ਪੰਜਾਬੀ, हिन्दी or English. This also sets the Gurbani script and the meaning language to suit: Gurmukhi with Punjabi meanings, Devanagari with Hindi meanings, or Gurmukhi with Roman under it and English meanings.

steps.title: Change the Gurbani script
steps.body: Reading › Gurbani script: Gurmukhi, Devanagari or Roman. In the reader, ਅ / अ / A at the top switches it at any time.

steps.title: Set the text in the reader
steps.body: Aa at the top of the reader opens Text settings: text size, Show meanings and their language, Roman under Gurmukhi, pause marks, Larivaar and more. Most of these are also under Settings › Reading.

tip: Elder mode is also offered during first run, on How do you like to read Gurbani? If your phone already uses large text, it starts switched on.

faq.q: Why did my Gurbani script change when I changed the language?
faq.a: Changing the app language also resets the script and the meaning language to that language’s defaults. Change the script back under Settings › Reading.

faq.q: Do reminders switch language too?
faq.a: Yes, the next time Hazri plans them: when you next open the app, or after your next paath or change to your goal.

faq.q: Where did the Vichar and Gurpurab cards go?
faq.a: Elder mode leaves them off Today to keep it simple. Turn Elder mode off to see them again.
